def-mis-em.title: EM
def-mis-em.html:
Given a current value 𝛉θ(s), define 𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉Q(θ∣θ(s))=E{ℓc(θ) | Dobs,θ(s)},{#eq-mis-expected-complete}

the expectation being over Dmis under the conditional density 𝛉f(Dmis∣Dobs,θ(s)). The E step computes 𝛉Q(⋅∣θ(s)); the M step sets 𝛉θ(s+1) to a maximizer of it. If the M step only increases Q, the scheme is called generalized EM.

def-mis-mechanisms.title: Missing completely at random, at random, not at random
def-mis-mechanisms.title_html: Missing completely at random, at random, not at random
def-mis-mechanisms.html:
Let D and R have the joint distribution @eq-mis-selection, and fix the realized values R=r and Dobs=a. The mechanism is

  1. missing completely at random (MCAR) if 𝛙𝛙f(r∣D,ψ)=f(r∣ψ) for every D and 𝛙ψ: the pattern is independent of the data, recorded or not;

  2. missing at random (MAR) if 𝛙f(r∣D,ψ) takes the same value for every D whose observed part is a, and every 𝛙ψ, so that it may be written 𝛙f(r∣a,ψ);

  3. missing not at random (MNAR) otherwise.

def-mis-multiple-imputation.title: Multiple imputation
def-mis-multiple-imputation.html:
Let 𝛄γ parameterize a model for the conditional distribution of Dmis given Dobs, with prior 𝛄p(γ). An imputation is proper in Rubin’s sense if the M completions are independent draws from 𝛄𝛄𝛄f(Dmis∣Dobs)=∫f(Dmis∣Dobs,γ)p(γ∣Dobs)dγ,{#eq-mis-posterior-predictive}

the posterior predictive distribution. Three standard constructions:

  1. Regression imputation with a parameter draw. For a continuous variable modelled as normal given the others, draw σ2∗=SSE/χk−q2 from its posterior under a flat prior, then 𝛄𝛄γ∗∼N(γ^,σ2∗(Zo⊤Zo)−1), then impute 𝛄z⊤γ∗+σ∗ε with ε standard normal. This is @thm-opt-bayes-conjugate with the noninformative limit @cor-opt-flat-prior.

  2. Predictive mean matching. Compute the predicted value for the record with the gap, find the d recorded records with the closest predicted values, and impute one of their observed values at random. Every imputed value then actually occurred, so the marginal distribution is respected even when the normal model is wrong, at the cost of a less transparent theory.

  3. Chained equations. With gaps in several variables, cycle through them, imputing each in turn from a regression on the current versions of all the others, for several sweeps, and keep the completion at the end of a sweep.

exm-mis-co2.title: A record with real gaps
exm-mis-co2.html:
The weekly averages of the continuous Mauna Loa record of atmospheric carbon dioxide run from March 1958 to December 2001 and cover 2284 weeks, of which 59 carry no value — 2.6% of the record, in 22 runs, the longest of 18 consecutive weeks.

They are not spread evenly. Before 1970, 8.6% of weeks are missing; from 1970 on, 0.4%, and a logistic regression of 1−Ri on calendar time multiplies the odds of a gap by 0.192 per decade. The mechanism depends on a variable recorded for every week, so the record is not MCAR.

Whether it is MAR given time is a question about the instrument, not about the numbers. The published rule is that a day contributes only if the analyser ran steadily for at least six hours, and a week with no such day contributes nothing. So the question is whether the analyser’s failure to deliver six steady hours is related to the concentration it would have read — plausibly not, if the failures are electrical or logistical; plausibly so, if unsettled air both disturbs the instrument and moves the reading. Nothing in Figure 41.1.1 can settle that.

exm-mis-co2-em.title: The Mauna Loa gaps
exm-mis-co2-em.html: Fit the trend-plus-harmonics model of Section 5.3 to all 2284 weeks, with the 59 missing ones handled by EM. The coefficients agree with the complete-case fit to machine precision, as @prp-mis-em-responses(c) requires, and the error standard deviation is 0.7992 ppm; filling in the gaps and treating them as data gives 0.7889 ppm, too small by the factor n/(n−m)=1.0132. The discrepancy is small here only because the gaps are few.

exm-mis-coverage.title: Five analyses of one problem
exm-mis-coverage.html:
Take n=200 records with two correlated covariates and y=1+0.5x1+0.6x2+ε, and lose x2 with a probability depending on x1 and y — both recorded, so MAR — leaving about 106 complete records. Over 2000 replicates, for the coefficient of x2:

Table 41.5.1. Five analyses of the same MAR problem. The estimand is β2=0.6; “mean se” is the average reported standard error and “sd” the actual spread of the estimates over 2000 replicates.

analysis bias mean se sd coverage
complete cases −0.151 0.101 0.102 67.2%
mean imputation −0.319 0.125 0.108 25.6%
single imputation −0.010 0.082 0.138 75.9%
multiple imputation, M=5 −0.013 0.118 0.119 95.0%
multiple imputation, M=20 −0.013 0.115 0.114 94.5%

Each row fails in its own way. The complete cases are biased, the missingness depending on the response. Mean imputation is far worse, and its reported standard error is larger than its actual spread. A single proper imputation removes the bias but reports a standard error three fifths of the truth, and covers 75.9% of the time. Multiple imputation with five draws gets both right, with an average estimated fraction of missing information 0.463 and median degrees of freedom 18.3.

exm-mis-em-covariate.title: An EM fit with a missing covariate
exm-mis-em-covariate.title_html: An EM fit with a missing covariate
exm-mis-em-covariate.html:
Simulate N=400 records with β1=0.8, and let the covariate be missing more often when the response is large; this loses 169 covariate values. The mechanism is MAR — it uses only the recorded y — so likelihood is valid and the complete-case fit is not. EM gives β^1=0.825; the complete cases give 0.620, attenuated by a quarter.

Figure 41.4.1 shows the two faces of the algorithm. The observed-data log-likelihood climbs monotonically, as @thm-mis-em(a) requires, and the distance to the fixed point falls by the constant factor 0.760 per sweep, matching to three decimals the largest eigenvalue of Ic−1Im below. Reaching eight decimal places takes 68 sweeps — slow by the standards of Newton’s method, which is the price of never differentiating an integral.

exm-mis-four-mechanisms.title: Four mechanisms, one regression
exm-mis-four-mechanisms.html:
Take yi=1+0.8xi+0.9wi+εi with xi,wi,εi independent standard normal and n=300, and lose the response under four mechanisms: completely at random; at random on x; at random on x and w; and not at random, on y.

Table 41.2.1. Mean complete-case estimate of β1=0.8 over 2000 replicates, for two analyses under four mechanisms.

mechanism complete cases fit y∼x fit y∼x+w
MCAR 194 0.801 0.801
MAR on x 181 0.804 0.802
MAR on x and w 178 0.637 0.800
MNAR on y 178 0.593 0.669

The first two rows are @prp-mis-complete-case(b): whatever the missingness does with x, the regression of y on x is untouched. The third is the warning attached to it. The mechanism is MAR, using only recorded variables, yet the short regression omitting w is badly biased, because selecting on w selects on the part of y that the short model calls error; adding w repairs it completely. The fourth row cannot be repaired by any choice of regressors, because the selection is on y itself.

exm-mis-pairwise.title: A correlation matrix with a negative eigenvalue
exm-mis-pairwise.title_html: A correlation matrix with a negative eigenvalue
exm-mis-pairwise.html: Twelve records on three variables, in three patterns of four: d3 absent in the first, d2 in the second, d1 in the third, with numbers chosen so that the available pairs give r12=0.9, r13=0.9 and r23=−0.9. Each is an ordinary correlation on its own four points; together they are impossible, since by @prp-rv-three-correlations the third must lie between 0.81−0.19×0.19=0.62 and 0.81+0.19=1. The matrix has smallest eigenvalue −0.800, so any procedure needing it to be nonnegative definite — a Cholesky factor, a GLS weight matrix, a normal likelihood — fails, even though the matrix itself is perfectly invertible.

exm-mis-survey.title: A survey that asks about income
exm-mis-survey.title_html: A survey that asks about income
exm-mis-survey.html: A survey records age x for everyone and income y for those who answer. Three stories. Completely at random: a printing fault left the income question off one batch of forms, assembled without regard to anything, so Pr(R=0∣x,y) is constant. At random: younger respondents skip the question more often, and among respondents of a given age, answering has nothing to do with earnings, so Pr(R=0∣x,y)=Pr(R=0∣x). Not at random: high earners skip the question at every age, so Pr(R=0∣x,y) depends on y even given x. The three are mutually exclusive descriptions of the world, and @prp-mis-untestable says the observed data cannot tell them apart.

exm-mis-tipping.title: How far must the assumption move?
exm-mis-tipping.title_html: How far must the assumption move?
exm-mis-tipping.html:
A two-arm study of 400 units records a baseline measurement for everyone and an outcome for those who stay. Dropout is likelier in the treated arm and at high baseline values, and 147 outcomes are lost — 83 treated and 64 control. Multiple imputation under MAR gives a treatment effect of 0.475 with 95% interval (0.199, 0.750).

Now suppose the treated units who dropped out would have done worse than the MAR imputation says, by δ. The estimate falls steadily and the lower limit reaches zero at δ∗=0.482, which is 0.452 of a residual standard deviation. The finding therefore survives the assumption that treated dropouts were up to about half a standard deviation worse than comparable stayers, and not more. Whether that is reassuring is a question for whoever knows why people dropped out.

exr-mis-bayes-equivalence.title: C1
exr-mis-bayes-equivalence.html: Show that when the imputation model and the analysis model are the same Bayesian model, Q¯ and T converge as M→∞ to the exact posterior mean and variance of Q given Dobs. Deduce that multiple imputation is, in the congenial case, a Monte Carlo scheme for a posterior that could also be sampled directly — and say why one might still prefer the imputation route.

exr-mis-cc-bias-normal.title: B1
exr-mis-cc-bias-normal.html: In @eq-mis-cc-bias take 𝛃y∣x∼N(x⊤β,σ2) and π(y,x)=Φ(a+by). Show that 𝛃𝛃E(y∣x,C=1)=x⊤β+bσ21+b2σ2ϕ(c)Φ(c),c=a+bx⊤β1+b2σ2, and deduce that the complete-case regression function is nonlinear in x whenever b≠0.

exr-mis-cc-mean.title: A1
exr-mis-cc-mean.html: Under the mechanism of @prp-mis-complete-case(b), show that the complete-case sample mean of y is generally not consistent for E(y), even though the complete-case regression coefficients are consistent. Reconcile the two statements.

exr-mis-cc-nonlinear.title: C1
exr-mis-cc-nonlinear.html: Let E(y∣x)=β0+β1x+β2x2 with β2≠0, and let the analyst fit a straight line. Show that even under @eq-mis-selection-on-x the complete-case slope generally differs from the full-data slope, and identify the functional of the covariate distribution that the straight-line slope estimates (see @thm-rv-blp and @thm-proj-blp). Under what selection would the two agree?

exr-mis-ccmv.title: C1
exr-mis-ccmv.html: For a monotone pattern with three time points, state the complete-case missing value restriction — the unidentified conditional for a unit that dropped out after time j equals the corresponding conditional among units seen at all three times — and the neighbouring-case alternative. Show that both are particular choices of the unidentified factor in @eq-mis-pm-marginal, and that the MAR choice lies between them in a sense you should make precise.

exr-mis-classify.title: A1
exr-mis-classify.html:
Classify each mechanism as MCAR, MAR or MNAR with respect to the recorded variables named.

  1. A blood assay is run on a random one-third of the samples chosen by a random number generator; age, sex and diagnosis are recorded for all.

  2. In a weight-loss trial, participants who have gained weight since the last visit stop attending. Weight at every previous visit is recorded.

  3. A scale reads “over range” and records nothing whenever the true weight exceeds 150 kg.

  4. A questionnaire item is missing for everyone interviewed by one interviewer, whose identity is recorded.

exr-mis-covariate-model.title: B2
exr-mis-covariate-model.html: A linear model has a single covariate x that is sometimes missing, with x∼N(μ,τ2) and y∣x∼N(β0+β1x,σ2). Write the observed-data likelihood contribution of a record with y recorded and x missing, and show that it is the density of a normal with mean β0+β1μ and variance β12τ2+σ2. Why does this contribution carry information about β1 even though it contains no x?

exr-mis-deflation-check.title: B2
exr-mis-deflation-check.html: Verify @eq-mis-deflation by simulation for n=300 and three missing fractions. Then show that the sample covariance of the filled column with a fully recorded variable w carries the same factor (k−1)/(n−1), and explain why the fraction recorded k/n is only the limiting form of it.

exr-mis-delta-bias.title: B1
exr-mis-delta-bias.html: For the model of @exm-mis-tipping, show analytically that the treatment effect estimated after a δ-shift of the treated arm’s imputations is τ^(δ)=τ^(0)−δp1, where p1 is the fraction of treated units whose outcome is missing, provided the analysis model contains the arm indicator. Check the slope against the figure.

exr-mis-distinct-fails.title: A1
exr-mis-distinct-fails.html: Give a mechanism under which MAR holds but the parameters are not distinct, and show that @eq-mis-factorization still holds while part (a) of @thm-mis-ignorable can fail. (Hint: let the probability of recording yi be a known function of 𝛃β.)

exr-mis-em-exponential-family.title: B2
exr-mis-em-exponential-family.html: Let the complete-data model be an exponential dispersion family (@def-glm-edf) with sufficient statistic t(D). Show that the E step reduces to computing 𝛉E{t(D)∣Dobs,θ(s)} and the M step to solving the complete-data likelihood equations with t replaced by that expectation. Why does the normal variance in @prp-mis-em-responses still require the extra term mσ2(s)?

exr-mis-em-not-max.title: C1
exr-mis-em-not-max.html: Construct a two-component normal mixture with missing labels — the classical EM problem — for which the likelihood is unbounded, and show that EM started near a degenerate configuration drives one variance to zero while the likelihood increases at every step. Reconcile this with @thm-mis-em(b).

exr-mis-em-variance-term.title: B1
exr-mis-em-variance-term.html: In @prp-mis-em-responses, suppose one carries out the iteration but omits the term mσ2(s) from the M step for the variance. Show that the coefficients are unaffected and that the variance converges to SSEo/n. Relate the discrepancy to @thm-dsn-missing(e).

exr-mis-em-zip.title: A1
exr-mis-em-zip.html: The EM algorithm for the zero-inflated model of Section 37.5 treats the component label as the missing datum. Identify Dmis, Q and the M step there, and check that @exr-cnt-em-monotone is the special case of @thm-mis-em(a).

exr-mis-ignorable-design.title: C1
exr-mis-ignorable-design.html: Show that @thm-dsn-missing is the special case of @thm-mis-ignorable in which the missing entries are responses, the mechanism depends only on the design, and the complete-data model is the normal linear model. Which part of @thm-dsn-missing corresponds to @eq-mis-observed-likelihood, and which to the warning that the degrees of freedom must be reduced?

exr-mis-little-test.title: B2
exr-mis-little-test.html: Two variables d1 (always recorded) and d2 (recorded when R=1). Propose a statistic with a known null distribution under MCAR and power against “the mechanism depends on d1”, and explain why no statistic can have power against “the mechanism depends on d2 given d1”.

exr-mis-mcar-implies-mar.title: A2
exr-mis-mcar-implies-mar.html: Show that MCAR implies MAR, and explain why no enlargement of Dobs can turn a MAR mechanism into an MNAR one.

exr-mis-mi-gamma.title: A2
exr-mis-mi-gamma.html: From @eq-mis-rubin-df, compute ν for M=5 and γ∈{0.1,0.3,0.5}. At which value of γ does the multiple-imputation reference distribution become so heavy-tailed that the interval is more than 20% wider than a normal-based one?

exr-mis-mi-single.title: A1
exr-mis-mi-single.html: Set M=1 in @thm-mis-rubin and explain why the formulas break down. Which of the three quantities in @eq-mis-rubin-pieces cannot be computed, and what does that say about single imputation?

exr-mis-monotone.title: B1
exr-mis-monotone.html: Let d=(d1,…,dq) have a monotone pattern, so that the recorded entries are d1,…,dK for some K∈{0,…,q}. Write the joint density of (d,K) using the chain rule f(d)=∏jf(dj∣d1,…,dj−1), and show that MAR is equivalent to Pr(K=k∣d) depending on d only through d1,…,dk.

exr-mis-normal-monotone.title: B1
exr-mis-normal-monotone.html: Let (ui,vi) be a bivariate normal sample with u recorded for all n units and v for the first k, the mechanism depending on u but not on v. Reparameterizing by (μu,σu2) and the regression parameters of v on u, derive the maximum likelihood estimates and the formula for μ^v quoted above. Extend to three variables with a monotone pattern: u recorded n times, v the first k2, z the first k3≤k2.

exr-mis-realized-mar.title: C1
exr-mis-realized-mar.html: Let the units be independent, each with d1∈{0,1} always recorded, and let d2 be recorded with probability p0 when d1=0 and with probability q(d2) when d1=1, where q is not constant. Show that @def-mis-mechanisms(b) fails at some patterns, but that on any sample in which no unit has d1=1 the realized-value condition holds exactly. What does this say about a frequentist argument, which averages over samples that did not occur, compared with a Bayesian one, which conditions on the sample in hand?

exr-mis-tipping-units.title: A2
exr-mis-tipping-units.html: In @exm-mis-tipping the tipping point is 0.482 on the outcome scale. Express it as a multiple of the estimated treatment effect and as a multiple of the residual standard deviation, and say which you would put in a report and why.

exr-mis-two-factorizations.title: A1
exr-mis-two-factorizations.html: Write the bivariate normal of @exr-mis-two-patterns in both factorizations, selection and pattern-mixture, and identify which parameters are estimable from the observed data in each. Why is the pattern-mixture form better suited to a sensitivity analysis?

exr-mis-two-patterns.title: B3
exr-mis-two-patterns.html: Let d=(d1,d2) be bivariate normal with mean (μ1,μ2) and covariance Σ, and let d2 be recorded with probability Φ(a+bd1). Show that the mechanism is MAR, compute E(d2∣R=1), and confirm that it differs from μ2 unless b=0 or σ12=0. Which class does the mechanism fall in if the probability is instead Φ(a+bd2)?

exr-mis-uncongenial.title: B1
exr-mis-uncongenial.html: Construct a simulation in which the analysis fits y on x1, x2 and their interaction, while x2 is imputed from a model without the interaction. Measure the bias in the interaction coefficient and its coverage. Then repeat with the interaction included in the imputation model.

exr-mis-weighted-unbiased.title: B3
exr-mis-weighted-unbiased.html: Prove that @eq-mis-weighted is an unbiased estimating equation when πi>0 for every unit, and show by example that the conclusion fails if πi=0 for a set of covariate values with positive probability. What does that failure correspond to in @prp-mis-complete-case?

exr-mis-worst-case.title: C2
exr-mis-worst-case.html: Suppose the response is bounded in [0,1]. Compute the worst-case bounds for its mean: impute every missing value by 0, then by 1. Show that the width of the resulting interval is the fraction missing, that it requires no assumption at all, and that it is usually too wide to be useful. Discuss where such bounds nevertheless earn their place.

prp-mis-complete-case.title: Validity of a complete-case analysis
prp-mis-complete-case.html:
Let the rows (d(i),Ci) be independent and identically distributed, with Pr(Ci=1)>0.

  1. (General condition.) Let a procedure estimate a functional T consistently at every law in a class containing both f, the law of d(i), and fC=1, its conditional law given Ci=1. Applied to the complete cases the procedure stays consistent for T(f) if and only if T(fC=1)=T(f). Under MCAR fC=1=f, and every such functional is preserved.

  2. (Regression with selection on the covariates.) Partition d(i)=(yi,x(i)) and suppose Pr(Ci=1∣yi,x(i))=Pr(Ci=1∣x(i))almost surely.{#eq-mis-selection-on-x}

    Then the conditional law of yi given x(i) is the same among the complete cases as in the population. So if a model specifies that conditional law correctly, the complete-case least squares estimate in a linear model is unbiased for 𝛃β conditionally on the selected covariates; and for a generalized linear model (@def-glm-model) the complete-case maximum likelihood estimate is consistent and asymptotically normal, with the usual model-based covariance of @thm-glm-asymptotics computed from the complete cases alone, provided their number grows and their covariate second moments converge to a nonsingular limit.

  3. (Otherwise.) If @eq-mis-selection-on-x fails, write π(y,x)=Pr(C=1∣y,x). The complete-case regression function is E(y∣x,C=1)=E(y∣x)+Cov{y,π(y,x)∣x}E{π(y,x)∣x},{#eq-mis-cc-bias}

    so the complete cases follow the intended regression function exactly when π is conditionally uncorrelated with the response at every x.

prp-mis-em-covariate.title: EM with a missing covariate
prp-mis-em-covariate.html:
Let xi∼N(μ,τ2) independently, and yi∣xi∼N(β0+β1xi,σ2), with 𝛉θ=(β0,β1,σ2,μ,τ2). Suppose yi is always recorded and xi is missing for a subset, with an ignorable mechanism. Then for a record with xi missing the E step uses E(xi∣yi)=μ+β1τ2β12τ2+σ2(yi−β0−β1μ),Var(xi∣yi)=τ2−β12τ4β12τ2+σ2,{#eq-mis-em-estep}

both evaluated at 𝛉θ(s), and the M step is the complete-data maximum likelihood fit with the sufficient statistics ∑ixi, ∑ixi2 and ∑ixiyi replaced by ∑iE(xi∣yi), ∑iE(xi2∣yi) and ∑iyiE(xi∣yi).

prp-mis-em-responses.title: EM for a normal linear model with missing responses
prp-mis-em-responses.title_html: EM for a normal linear model with missing responses
prp-mis-em-responses.html:
Let 𝛃𝛆y=Xβ+ε with 𝛆ε∼Nn(0,σ2I) and rank(X)=p; let the responses of a set of m rows be unrecorded, the covariates of those rows being known, with an ignorable mechanism, and suppose the observed rows Xo have rank p. Write SSEo for the residual sum of squares of the least squares fit on the observed rows. Then:

  1. the E step replaces each missing yi by 𝛃x(i)⊤β(s) in the cross-product terms of ℓc, and each yi2 by 𝛃(x(i)⊤β(s))2+σ2(s);

  2. the M step is 𝛃β(s+1)=(X⊤X)−1X⊤y(s) with y(s) the completed vector, and 𝛃σ2(s+1)=n−1{‖y(s)−Xβ(s+1)‖2+mσ2(s)};

  3. the unique fixed point is 𝛃𝛃β∗=β^o, the least squares estimate from the observed rows, and σ2∗=SSEon−m,{#eq-mis-em-sigma}

    which is the observed-data maximum likelihood estimate, based on n−m observations.

prp-mis-louis.title: The missing-information principle
prp-mis-louis.html:
At any 𝛉θ, with Sc the complete-data score, 𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉∂ℓ∂θ=E(Sc∣Dobs,θ),Io=E(−∂Sc/∂θ⊤∣Dobs,θ)−Var(Sc∣Dobs,θ).{#eq-mis-louis}

Consequently 𝛉Im=Var(Sc∣Dobs,θ) is nonnegative definite: the observed information is never larger than the expected complete-data information.

prp-mis-mean-imputation.title: Mean imputation deflates the variance
prp-mis-mean-imputation.html:
Let z1,…,zn be independent and identically distributed with finite variance σ2, of which k are recorded and n−k missing, the mechanism being completely at random; let z~i equal zi when recorded and z¯obs otherwise. Then the sample variance of the filled column satisfies E{1n−1∑i=1n(z~i−z~¯)2 | k}=k−1n−1σ2,{#eq-mis-deflation}

so the estimate of σ2 is too small by the factor (k−1)/(n−1)≈k/n, the proportion recorded.

prp-mis-sensitivity.title: Selection and pattern-mixture models
prp-mis-sensitivity.html:
Consider a single variable v recorded when R=1, alongside always recorded variables u.

  1. Every selection model f(v∣u)Pr(R=1∣v,u) corresponds to the pattern-mixture model with f(v∣u,R=r)∝f(v∣u)Pr(R=r∣v,u),Pr(R=r∣u)=∫f(v∣u)Pr(R=r∣v,u)dv, and conversely, so neither formulation is more general.

  2. The observed data identify f(v∣u,R=1) and Pr(R=1∣u), and nothing about f(v∣u,R=0). The marginal f(v∣u)= Pr(R=1∣u)f(v∣u,R=1)+ Pr(R=0∣u)f(v∣u,R=0){#eq-mis-pm-marginal}

    is therefore identified only after the analyst supplies the last factor. Missing at random is the supply f(v∣u,R=0)=f(v∣u,R=1).

  3. Let the mechanism be Pr(R=1∣v,u)=h{a(u)+cv}, with h continuous, strictly increasing and valued in (0,1) and a(⋅) an unrestricted function. Then c is not identified: for every c at which the tilt @eq-mis-tilt below is integrable and its integral covers the required value, there are an a(⋅) and an f(v∣u,R=0) reproducing the observed-data distribution exactly. Any standard error reported for c comes from restricting a(⋅) — to a+u⊤b, say — and from the assumed forms of h and f(v∣u), not from the data.

prp-mis-untestable.title: The observed data do not identify the mechanism
prp-mis-untestable.title_html: The observed data do not identify the mechanism
prp-mis-untestable.html:
Let d=(d1,d2) be a unit’s record, with d1 always recorded and d2 recorded exactly when R=1. The distribution of the observed data is determined by the three pieces f(d1), Pr(R=1∣d1) and f(d2∣d1,R=1), and determines nothing else. Consequently:

  1. for every conditional density g(d2∣d1) there is exactly one joint distribution of (d,R) with the given observed-data distribution and with f(d2∣d1,R=0)=g(d2∣d1);

  2. one of these choices, g=f(⋅∣d1,R=1), is MAR; every other is MNAR; and all assign the observed data the same likelihood.

thm-mis-em.title: The EM sequence never decreases the likelihood
thm-mis-em.title_html: The EM sequence never decreases the likelihood
thm-mis-em.html:
Let 𝛉θ(s+1) satisfy 𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉Q(θ(s+1)∣θ(s))≥Q(θ(s)∣θ(s)). Then

  1. 𝛉𝛉ℓ(θ(s+1))≥ℓ(θ(s)), with equality only if 𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛉Q(θ(s+1)∣θ(s))=Q(θ(s)∣θ(s)) and the two conditional densities of Dmis agree almost everywhere;

  2. if ℓ is bounded above, 𝛉ℓ(θ(s)) converges;

  3. if Q(⋅∣⋅) is differentiable in its first argument and 𝛉θ(s+1) is an interior maximizer, then at any fixed point 𝛉θ∗ of the iteration the observed-data score vanishes: 𝛉𝛉𝛉∂ℓ(θ)/∂θ|θ∗=0.

thm-mis-ignorable.title: Ignorability
thm-mis-ignorable.html:
Suppose that

  1. the mechanism is MAR at the realized (R,Dobs) in the sense of @def-mis-mechanisms(b);

  2. the parameters are distinct: the parameter space of 𝛉𝛙(θ,ψ) is a product set Θ×Ψ, so that knowing one places no restriction on the other.

Then the full likelihood factors, 𝛉𝛙𝛉𝛙Lfull(θ,ψ)=L(θ)⋅f(R∣Dobs,ψ),{#eq-mis-factorization}

and consequently:

  1. the maximizer of Lfull in 𝛉θ is the maximizer of L, and likelihood ratio statistics for hypotheses about 𝛉θ alone are the same under both;

  2. if the prior is 𝛉𝛙𝛉𝛙p(θ,ψ)=p(θ)p(ψ), the posterior of 𝛉θ given (Dobs,R) equals its posterior given Dobs alone, computed from @eq-mis-observed-likelihood;

  3. if in addition the MAR condition holds at every (R,Dobs), the observed-data score has mean zero and the usual maximum likelihood asymptotics (@thm-opt-mle) apply to L under the ordinary regularity conditions.

A mechanism satisfying (i) and (ii) is called ignorable.

thm-mis-rubin.title: Combining M analyses
thm-mis-rubin.html:
Let Q be the estimand and suppose the complete-data analysis is calibrated in the sense that, given the complete data D, it reports Q^(D) and U(D) with E(Q∣D)=Q^(D),Var(Q∣D)=U(D).{#eq-mis-complete-calibration}

Let D(1),…,D(M) be independent draws from @eq-mis-posterior-predictive, generated by the analyst and therefore conditionally independent of Q given Dobs; put Q^ℓ=Q^(D(ℓ)) and Uℓ=U(D(ℓ)), and define Q¯=1M∑ℓQ^ℓ,U¯=1M∑ℓUℓ,B=1M−1∑ℓ(Q^ℓ−Q¯)2.{#eq-mis-rubin-pieces}

Then, with all expectations conditional on Dobs:

  1. (Decomposition.) Var(Q∣Dobs)=E(U∣Dobs)+Var(Q^∣Dobs), and U¯ and B are unbiased for the two terms;

  2. (Total variance.) Q¯ is unbiased for E(Q∣Dobs), and T=U¯+(1+1M)B{#eq-mis-rubin-total}

    is unbiased for the variance of Q−Q¯ given Dobs;

  3. (Degrees of freedom.) treating U¯ as fixed and (M−1)B/Var(Q^∣Dobs) as χM−12, the variance of T matches that of a scaled χν2 variable with ν=(M−1){T(1+M−1)B}2=M−1γ2,γ=(1+M−1)BT,{#eq-mis-rubin-df}

    and the interval Q¯±tν,1−α/2T is the standard multiple-imputation interval; γ is the estimated fraction of missing information;

  4. (Efficiency.) write T∞=E(U)+Var(Q^) for the total variance at M=∞ and γ∞=Var(Q^)/T∞ for the limiting fraction of missing information. Then the target of T exceeds T∞ by the factor 1+γ∞/M, so using M imputations rather than infinitely many inflates the standard error by (1+γ∞/M)1/2.
